newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX 3B VENTURA OUT 3-4 MONTHS WITH BROKEN LEG.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX 3B VENTURA OUT 3-4 MONTHS WITH BROKEN LEG.

text.p: Chicago White Sox veteran third baseman Robin Ventura will be sidelined three to four months after fracturing his right leg and dislocating his right ankle while sliding into home plate during an exhibition game against the Boston Red Sox Friday night.

Ventura was carried from the field and had his ankle put back into place in the clubhouse before he was taken to the hospital, where X-rays revealed a compound fracture of his right tibia and fibula, a team spokesman said.
"Knowing Robin and his work habits, hopefully he can come back before (four months)," White Sox general manager Ron Schueler said.

The injury occurred in the bottom of the fourth inning. Ventura walked and was at second base with two out when he tried to score on Ray Durham's single. He slid awkwardly into the plate and was tagged out.
"I saw it and it wasn't pretty," Schueler said of the injury, which required surgery.
"It was a dislocation and a fracture and the ligaments went with it. (The bone) came through the skin. They repaired it and inserted a screw. In six weeks, he can start rehabbing."
The 29-year-old Ventura has been a mainstay in the White Sox lineup since 1990. He hit .287 last season and posted career highs with 34 homers and 105 RBI.
